title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono visit Keith Richards in France | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono visited The Rolling Stones’ guitarist Keith Richards in Villefranche-sur-Mer, France, on 19 May 1971.

Lennon and Ono had spent several days in the French Riviera, attending the Cannes Film Festival and the premieres of their films Fly and Apotheosis.

Richards was in France as a tax exile, renting Nellcôte, a villa in Villefranche-sur-Mer on the Côte d’Azur in southern France, which had been converted into a recording studio. Photographer Dominic Tarlé was staying at the villa and remembered Lennon and Ono’s visit.

John Lennon came once, but just for one afternoon. He was in the South of France to visit an art exhibition in Nice with Yoko. I didn’t take a picture of them, somehow it wasn’t right. As soon as he came, he went off to Keith’s bedroom for about three quarters of an hour. Then he came downstairs to say ‘goodbye,’ vomited on the carpet and left.
Dominic Tarlé
Exile
